intuition.title: Study context: A measured core and qualified later treatments
intuition.text: One seven-minute CdSe core preparation has an approximately 4 nm product. ZnS shell growth and later ligand treatments are source-described supporting processes; missing seed amount, shell dimensions and specimen-specific exchange charges remain visible.
intuition.source_locator: SI PDF p. 4–6, CdSe synthesis and cleaning; SI PDF p. 5–7, Shell growth and exchange

intuition.title: Study context: Surface bonding is a spectroscopic model
intuition.text: NMR, released molecular products and XPS support anionic X-type ligand binding to a Cd-rich surface. The authors distinguish this model from a universally proven nanocrystal surface structure; no atomic coordinates, crystal polymorph or surface site map are provided.

intuition.title: Study context: Adsorption and substitution differ
intuition.text: Unprotected thiols bind while retaining phosphonate; added triethylamine promotes displacement. Protected thiol and chloride reagents cleave phosphonate directly. Spectral changes and colloidal behavior are not additional particle-size measurements.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2, Schemes 2–3 and thiol experiments

bindings.caption: Mix diethylzinc and TOP using the source mass and mole labels; freeze. The 0.608 g/0.492 mmol stock pair is internally inconsistent with the later aliquot label, and remains unresolved. Equipment geometry is illustrative; exact source conditions are retained in the operation.

Mix bis(trimethylsilyl)sulfide and TOP using both source quantities without correcting their disagreement with the later aliquot label. Equipment geometry is illustrative; exact source conditions are retained in the operation.

Load source TOPO/ODPA charges in a 50 mL three-neck flask with stirbar, thermocouple adaptor, condenser and septum; vigorously stir at 100 °C under vacuum for at least 30 min. Equipment geometry is illustrative; exact source conditions are retained in the operation.
Admit Ar, heat to 275 °C and add 1.0 g zinc stock, labelled 0.492 mmol Zn, dropwise; then lower to 250 °C. Equipment geometry is illustrative; exact source conditions are retained in the operation.

Dissolve dry CdSe cores of unreported mass in 1.000 g (2.70 mmol) TOP and inject under argon at the source 250 °C stage. Equipment geometry is illustrative; exact source conditions are retained in the operation.

bindings.source_locator: SI PDF p. 6, Cleaning CdSe and CdSe/ZnS
bindings.caption: Below 100 °C dilute with dry degassed acetone to 50 mL total volume. Transfer under argon into the glovebox and centrifuge the milky suspension; speed and dwell are unspecified. Equipment geometry is illustrative; exact source conditions are retained in the operation.

bindings.source_locator: SI PDF p. 6, Cleaning CdSe and CdSe/ZnS
bindings.caption: Redissolve in 15 mL anhydrous chloroform, add 5 mL octylamine, then acetone to 50 mL total volume; immediately centrifuge to collect the nanocrystal film. Equipment geometry is illustrative; exact source conditions are retained in the operation.

bindings.source_locator: SI PDF p. 6, Cleaning CdSe and CdSe/ZnS
bindings.caption: Dissolve the film in 15 mL hexane. Add acetone slowly until precipitation, shake/sonicate to redissolve, and repeat dropwise until the solid no longer clears. Discard this solid and retain the colored supernatant. Equipment geometry is illustrative; exact source conditions are retained in the operation.

bindings.source_locator: SI PDF p. 6, Cleaning CdSe and CdSe/ZnS
bindings.caption: Add further acetone to the colored supernatant to precipitate nanocrystals. Repeat the hexane/acetone fractional-precipitation step a second time. Unreported antisolvent volumes and centrifugation settings remain unknown. Equipment geometry is illustrative; exact source conditions are retained in the operation.

general_background.title: Destabilizing a particle dispersion
general_background.summary: An antisolvent can solvate a particle's ligand shell less favourably than the original dispersion medium. Reduced solvation can weaken colloidal stability and allow particles to aggregate and separate from the liquid, depending on the ligands and solvent mixture.
